newsitem.title: UK: Regulators dissect Morgan Grenfell in funds probe.
newsitem.headline: Regulators dissect Morgan Grenfell in funds probe.

text.p: Investigators from Britain's fund management industry regulator are carrying out a detailed dissection of Morgan Grenfell Asset Management's trading as part of a probe into "irregularities", industry sources said on Friday.

The Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) has a team inside the London-based fund management arm of Deutsche Bank which, one source said, "...is looking at every trade done by every fund manager".

Fund managers will be hoping they have played by the rules because the investigation is likely to turn up even relatively small misdemeanours and, in the current climate, breaches are unlikely to be ignored.

IMRO is investigating the activities of Morgan Grenfell fund manager Peter Young who was suspended earlier this week and had his personal assets frozen while the probe into his management of the funds is conducted.
Trading in three funds managed by MGAM was temporarily halted this week following Young's suspension.
Sources said a team of at least six investigators from IMRO's Enforcement Division is in place to carry out a painstaking probe.
The sources said that this made for a more diffcult climate for anyone else alleged to have broken any rules.
Another MG fund manager, Stewart Armer, was suspended on Wednesday in a separate case from Young's, because of an alleged unrelated breach of personal account dealing rules.
Before his suspension, Young had invested heavily in speculative high-technology stocks, many of which were not listed on stock exchanges.
Banking sources said Young's holdings had exceeded the maximum 10 percent limit on such unlisted stocks and he had been ordered to reduce them to five percent.

Rather than reduce the holdings, however, Young is alleged by Morgan Grenfell to have set up more unlisted holding companies, in which some of the original investments were then held, according to remarks attributed to the investment bank in a report in London's Financial Times newspaper.
Young was not available on Friday to comment on Morgan Grenfell's statement.

Sources close to IMRO said the investigation process is unlikely to be a quick one and it will not pass its file to Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO), which 1nvestigates complex fraud cases, unless it is clear criminal charges are likely.
There could be several repercussions from the investigation, either criminal charges or disciplinary action by IMRO.

After a five-month inquiry, IMRO last month fined securities house Jardine Fleming 700,000 pounds ($1.10 million) and Jardine Fleming Asset Management lost its authorisation after repeated flouting of rules.
"The assumption that the SFO is going to get involved is a bit misleading," said one source. "They may, but on the other hand, they may not." ($1=.6385 Pound)
